question: When pulling doubles or triples, which trailer is most likely to turn over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect?
choice_c: The last trailer in the combination
explanation: The manual states that doubles and triples are more likely to turn over because of the crack-the-whip effect, and the last trailer in a combination is most likely to turn over.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Converter dollies built on or after what date are required to have antilock brakes?
explanation: The manual states that converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have antilock brakes, and these dollies have a yellow lamp on the left side.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: On a converter dolly equipped with antilock brakes, where is the required indicator lamp located?
choice_a: On the right side of the dolly
choice_b: On top of the dolly frame
choice_c: On the left side of the dolly
choice_d: On the rear of the dolly only
explanation: The manual states these dollies (built on or after March 1, 1998) will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: For the safest handling on the road when coupling twin trailers, where should the more heavily loaded semitrailer be positioned?
choice_b: In first position behind the tractor
explanation: The manual states that for the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in first position behind the tractor, with the lighter trailer in the rear.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A hydraulic jack used to lift trailers for maintenance
choice_b: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination
choice_c: A brake control valve mounted in the cab
choice_d: A device that measures liquid surge in tank trailers
explanation: The manual defines a converter gear on a dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: Before backing a converter dolly under a rear trailer, the trailer height must be:
choice_a: Exactly level with the top of the fifth wheel
choice_b: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
choice_c: Slightly higher than the fifth wheel so it drops onto the dolly
choice_d: It does not matter as long as the landing gear is lowered
explanation: The manual states trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When making a visual check of a fifth wheel coupling, what should you look for?
choice_a: A small amount of space between the upper and lower fifth wheel
choice_b: No visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel, with locking jaws closed on the kingpin
explanation: The manual instructs making a visual check of the coupling to confirm no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on the kingpin.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: Why should you never unlock the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: It will damage the fifth wheel
choice_b: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it difficult to re-couple
choice_c: It will cause the air brakes to lock
explanation: The manual warns never to unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: When inspecting a set of doubles, the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer should be:
explanation: The manual specifies that shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: When checking the lower fifth wheel during inspection, the locking jaws should be closed around:
choice_b: The shank of the kingpin, not the head
explanation: The manual specifies checking that locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: During the air brake check, the trailer air supply (tractor protection valve) control should pop out to the emergency position when air pressure falls into what range specified by the manufacturer?
choice_a: Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi
choice_b: Usually within the range of 60 to 80 psi
choice_c: Usually within the range of 5 to 10 psi
choice_d: Usually within the range of 100 to 120 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control should pop out when air pressure falls into the range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4

question: How do you test that a trailer's emergency brakes are working?
choice_a: Listen for air escaping at the front of the tractor
choice_b: Charge the trailer air brake system, put the trailer air supply control in the emergency position, then pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to check that the emergency brakes are on
choice_c: Check that the trailer rolls freely with the parking brake set
choice_d: Apply the foot brake only and watch the brake lights
explanation: The manual describes charging the trailer air brake system, then pulling out the trailer air supply control (placing it in the emergency position) and pulling gently on the trailer with the tractor to check that the trailer emergency brakes are on.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4
